content.value:
A Pose represents a robot's full 2D state: where it is and which direction it faces.

new Pose(x, y, heading)

X — forward position (positive = forward).

Y — lateral position (positive = left).

Heading — orientation. Use Math.toRadians(degrees).

Examples:

new Pose(0, 0, Math.toRadians(0)) — origin, facing right.

new Pose(24, 12, Math.toRadians(90)) — 24" forward, 12" left, facing up.

new Pose(36, -12, Math.toRadians(45)) — 36" forward, 12" right, facing 45°.

Getters: pose.getX(), pose.getY(), pose.getHeading().

content.question: A robot starts at (0, 0) facing 0°. You want it to go 20" behind it, still facing 0°. What is the target Pose?

content.value:
0° = +X (right)
90° = +Y (up)
180° = -X (left)
-90° or 270° = -Y (down)

Use Math.toRadians() — Pedro Pathing expects radians internally.

Field-centric — X and Y are fixed to the field. (5, 10) always means the same spot.

Robot-centric — axes move with the robot. (5, 0) means 5" in front of wherever the robot faces.

Pedro Pathing paths are field-centric. A waypoint at (24, 0) means 24" forward on the field, not 24" in front of the robot.

The Follower converts between the two internally using the robot's current heading.

In competition, you write one autonomous and need it to work on both the red and blue alliances. The field is symmetrical — the blue side is a mirror of the red side.

Instead of writing two different autos, use mirroring:

Pose mirrored = pose.mirror();

The mirror() method flips the X coordinate across the field center (defaults to 141.5). Heading is automatically adjusted to face the mirrored direction.

Pattern: store your poses in an array, then call .mirror() on each one when you're on the red alliance. One set of waypoints, both alliances.
